Priya: customer-reported: streaming responses abruptly cut around ~2-3s, client sees ECONNRESET and we recorded a 5xx. ticket: #6821, acct: acme-inc. logs attached. :frowning:
Sam: can you paste the gateway logs and the client-side stacktrace? is this reproducible?
Priya: small snippets below. gateway shows EOF on socket and we incremented gateway_5xx_total. customer says they did not get billed for 0 tokens but for partial request which is causing dispute. repro rate ~1/100 requests on their workload.
Priya: ```
[proxy] 2026-03-05T14:12:03Z INFO conn 0x7ff: read 1024 bytes
[proxy] 2026-03-05T14:12:03Z ERROR conn 0x7ff: unexpected EOF while reading chunked body, marking upstream as 5xx
[gateway] 2026-03-05T14:12:03Z WARN stream 0x12: client reset (RST_STREAM)
```
Sam: looks like we classify any socket EOF while response streaming as a 5xx. that's noisy for mid-stream client-initiated half-close.
Marta: I can repro locally using a small curl client that half-closes after first few chunks. repro command: ```
printf 'data: {"prompt":"hello"}\n' | curl -v -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  --data-binary @- --keepalive-time 2 && sleep 1; kill -9 $PID_CLIENT
```
Marta: server reacts with EOF and proxy logs the same error.
Dave: billing here — customer was charged for 4.2 tokens on that request even though their client aborted. they want refund for those 12 requests flagged in ticket. is the billing pipeline counting any streamed response that started as billable even if connection aborted?
Priya: our metering counts tokens as they're emitted by runtime. but if client disconnects mid-stream we should not mark request as 5xx for SLA/billing classification. currently downstream metric increments 5xx which triggers automated refunds and alerts incorrectly.
Sam: quick mitigation: change classification rule to only increment gateway_5xx_total when upstream returned explicit 5xx status or the proxy returned a TCP reset we initiated, not for client-initiated halfclose. we can flip a flag in prod routing layer. low-risk.
ops-bot: deploy: canary/route-classify-fix started by sam at 2026-03-05T15:20:00Z :rocket:
Priya: can we also add a small log tag to indicate client-initiated halfclose vs upstream error so billing can filter from historical? e.g., `classification=client_disconnect`
Marta: ack — I'll add the log tag and a unit test for the chunked EOF path.
Dave: after mitigation, I'll run the refund script for the 12 disputed charges and put an escrow hold while engineering confirms root cause.
Sam: filing ENG-RUNTIME-1123, notes: streaming chunked EOF handling, avoid counting client halfclose as 5xx, add log tag, short-term flag gate. assigning to eng-runtime oncall.
Priya: @Sam please also add repro steps + curl snippet to the ticket. I'll notify customer that we're deploying a fix and will follow up on refund. :eyes:
Dave: thanks all. I'll keep billing in the loop. :thumbsup:
Marta: leaving a bookmark for follow-up: add an e2e test with intermittent client resets, and a gate to roll the classification change over 1h canary.
Sam: agree. closing the loop after canary looks stable (1% traffic window).
Priya: updating ticket and marking as escalated to eng-runtime. thanks.
